plain: Unwillingness; a lack of desire to do something.

webster.text: Disinclination; aversion; unwillingness; dislike; as the indisposition of men to submit to severe discipline; an indisposition to abandon vicious practices.

example.quote: If a general declaration would satisfy any gentleman he had no indisposition to declare his sentiments.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, July 13, 1787
